--- page 1 ---
Factors in Recall
Several everyday habits change how much a student remembers after a week.
The habits below were compared in a small invented study.
These differences are modest, but they add up across a whole term of study.
--- page 2 ---
Study Habits That Work
Four habits are worth building early in a course.
1. Test yourself on a topic before you reread it, because recall practice strengthens memory.
2. Space your sessions over several days instead of packing them into one evening.
3. Explain each idea aloud in your own words as if teaching a friend.
4. Sleep well after studying so that the new material has time to settle.
--- page 3 ---
Why These Habits Work
Each habit makes the brain work a little harder at the moment of learning.
That effort leaves a stronger trace.
Easy study feels pleasant but leaves a weaker one.
Students often judge their learning by how familiar the page feels.
Familiarity is a poor guide, which is why self-testing is worth the discomfort.
--- page 4 ---
That completes the chapter on remembering well.
The next chapter turns to attention.
--- page 5 ---
Next chapter
Attention decides what the mind takes in.
Without it, little is stored at all.
